bugs.name: Customer Boolean attribute Yes filter leaves False customers visible
bugs.summary: Applying the customer-type boolean attribute filter “is Yes” repeatedly leaves both the True and False customers visible and the count at 2.
bugs.expected: With the i3 attr boolean condition set to “is Yes,” only the customer whose boolean value is True should remain in the filtered list; the False customer should be excluded.
bugs.actual: After applying the visible Attribute → i3 attr boolean → is → Yes condition twice, the list still showed both “MoBoolFilterQ731 False” and “MoBoolFilterQ731 True,” with the i3-attr-records count remaining 2.
reproSteps: Sign in to the supplied Saleor dashboard through its authorized fixture authentication setup.

Through the normal UI, prepare an owned customer type with a Boolean attribute and the other reported attribute kinds. Save two customers in that type with persisted Boolean True and False values and distinct identifying names.

Open the type-scoped Customers list and use a shared search marker to show both customers. Open Filters and select Attribute > Boolean > is > Yes. Selecting the condition alone leaves both rows visible.

The reported final native preview attempted to apply the filter, but its locator selected the expanded Filters toggle, not the actual Apply button. Closing or reopening that dropdown does not commit the condition.
As the independent countercheck, click the actual visible Apply button (save-filters-button). The normal UI request contains boolean:true and only the persisted True customer remains with count 1.

Reopen Filters and verify Yes remains selected and the unchanged Apply button is disabled. No claim is made that the original native type flags or every possible Boolean-filter path were exhaustively reproduced.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected this native report because the final alleged Apply action selected the Filters dropdown toggle (element 145, filters-button), not the actual Apply button (element 184, save-filters-button). The trace and tool result are correlated by the unique customer search marker, paired True/False rows, selected element and tool interval. A fresh independent UI check reproduced the reported customer-type and persisted-value prerequisites: selecting Yes alone kept both rows; a real pointer click on Apply sent boolean:true and retained only the True row with count 1. Reopening retained Yes, with unchanged Apply disabled. The supplied report therefore does not establish a Boolean-filter application defect. The first native attempt was not separately traced, original type property flags were unspecified, and this rejection does not assert that every possible Boolean-filter path works.

matchingGuidance.rejectionScope: The supplied report says False customers remained after applying Attribute Boolean is Yes. Its final alleged Apply action targeted the Filters dropdown toggle rather than the commit button.
